answer: Audit every verdict through escalating juries where each appeal redraws twice the jurors and the losing appellant pays, so defending a captured opal gets exponentially expensive. One honest agent appeals rarely and holds 100 credits of unspent fees. A farm overturning 50 rulings against its river clones pays a doubling bill every round, reaching 5,600 credits by the sixth appeal, so 50 clones cost 56 times one. The failure mode is cost falling on honest appellants, so the deposit must refund on success and the relic must stay small for first appeals.
